payload.content_text: Resolve this stockout efficiently. ProcurementAgent wants to order from the cheapest supplier. LogisticsAgent wants to use the fastest shipping method. FinanceAgent wants to minimise total spend. Each agent is pulling in a different direction and the stockout is not resolved — either the order is delayed or costs spike unexpectedly. The agents must agree on what efficiently means in this context, on the relative priority of cost versus speed, and on a supplier and shipping selection framework that all three can apply consistently to resolve the stockout without creating new cost or delay problems.

issues: relative priority of cost versus speed

efficiently: minimise delays while keeping costs reasonable
achieve resolution within a predefined timeframe
cheapest supplier: supplier with the lowest unit price
supplier with the lowest total cost including shipping
supplier with the lowest cost for urgent orders
minimise total spend: reduce both procurement and shipping costs
relative priority of cost versus speed: cost is more important than speed
speed is more important than cost
cost and speed are equally important
prioritise based on urgency of stockout
supplier and shipping selection framewor: select supplier first, then shipping method
select shipping method first, then supplier
evaluate supplier and shipping method together
use a scoring system to balance cost and speed
